video.title: The Most Overlooked $1M Business Every Town Needs

summary: Chris Koerner tours Laundry Spot's flagship store in Hamilton, Ohio with co-owner Tyler. The family business builds large, modern laundromats with cloud-controlled washers, direct soap injection and any-payment options, priced at parity with old competitors; the Hamilton store did about $1.025M revenue and $420k profit last year. Tyler shares startup costs ($1.2M-$2.2M excluding real estate), site selection, a grand-opening playbook with two free-laundry weekends, commercial laundry at $1-$3/lb, and the new franchise (36 units in 8 months). Key takeaway: build new, better stores rather than buying old ones, and remove every bit of friction for customers.

speakers.name: Tyler
speakers.description: Co-owner of Laundry Spot (family laundromat business with father-in-law David), finance background

ideas.name: Modern large-format laundromat (Laundry Spot)
ideas.one_liner: Build new, large (4,400-8,000 sq ft) laundromats with high-efficiency cloud-controlled washers, priced at parity with local competitors, to take over a mid-size town.
ideas.business_model: Self-service wash/dry revenue plus loyalty card, wash-and-fold, commercial laundry and dry cleaning; now franchising
ideas.customer: Residents of mid-size towns (e.g. Hamilton, Ohio, ~60k people), especially renters in older apartments with poor shared laundry; families
ideas.problem: Existing laundromats are old, dirty, inefficient and owner-centric
ideas.offer: Clean, large stores with giant washers (up to 130 lb), direct soap injection with 8 options, ozone cycles, any payment method, nice bathrooms, 40+ cameras

pricing.notes: Utilities under 10% of revenue vs 20-30% for old stores; dryers 10-15% of washer revenue; priced same or lower than competitors.

tactics.name: Laundromat grand opening playbook
steps: 3 months out: coming-soon EDDM mailers, join chambers, publications
1 month out: VIP red-carpet event for local business owners (few thousand dollars)
Announce free laundry weekends at 1 month and 2 weeks
Run two consecutive free weekends, all staff present, ask every customer for a Google review

quote.text: how many fivestar reviews can we get as quickly as possible?
quote.speaker: Tyler

tactics.name: Site selection
steps: Look for areas with 3-5 existing laundromats (proven market)
Hang out at competitors, take water meter readings to estimate revenue, note pricing
Match demographics; target 1990s apartments with poor shared laundry, not new builds
Build next to or across from the best competitor

quote.text: We don't want new. We want the apartment. We want the 1990s apartment
quote.speaker: Tyler

tactics.name: Price at parity with better experience
steps: Use efficient equipment to keep utilities <10% so you can match prices
Offer a much better experience at the same price

tactics.name: Use machine data to pick equipment
steps: Track every cycle per machine in the cloud
Compare turns per day by machine size
Add more large machines where the data shows demand

tactics.name: Accept every payment method
steps: Quarters, loyalty card, debit/credit, Apple Pay, tap
Reward loyalty card with free dry credits

warnings.warning: Buying an old laundromat: books are unverifiable, people overpay, equipment breaks constantly, and you buy yourself a low-paying job.

quote.text: a lot of people who fall into that trap find themselves that they just bought themselves a job, like a lowpaying job
quote.speaker: Tyler

warnings.warning: Laundromats are not passive; even with a GM and AGM it's work.

quote.text: nothing is passive. I mean, we have a GM and an AGM and still not passive
quote.speaker: Tyler

warnings.warning: Car washes go fully down when a part fails; laundromats keep earning with machines down.

quote.text: With my laundry mats over here, I can have 1 2 3 five machines down, I'm still making money
quote.speaker: Tyler

warnings.warning: Short leases risk the landlord taking over your build-out; get long leases with options.

quote.text: You don't want the landlord to be able to just kick you out
quote.speaker: Tyler

warnings.warning: Influencer hype around laundromats glosses over these problems.

lessons.lesson: Build new rather than buy and refurbish; you can outcompete old stores from across the street.

quote.text: why would we buy this, put all this money to fix it up when I could just go across the street
quote.speaker: Tyler

lessons.lesson: Remove all friction from receiving money; serve what the customer wants, not what is easy for the owner.

quote.text: You got to remove all the friction of receiving money
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Mid-size towns with low competition quality can be dominated with a few great locations.

quote.text: The the competition, the bar is so low
quote.speaker: Tyler

lessons.lesson: Get people in the door free; habit-driven customers don't go back once they've switched.

quote.text: Literally, if we just get people in the door, they're not going back
quote.speaker: Tyler

lessons.lesson: A/B test business model choices across locations (card-only vs coin-only).

quote.text: He literally had an AB test
quote.speaker: Tyler

lessons.lesson: Efficient equipment lowers variable cost, enabling price parity with a better product.
Self-service matures in years 2-3 as the 1-3 mile radius saturates; growth then comes from commercial and price rises.
Bonus depreciation on equipment makes laundromats attractive for offsetting other income (US).

quote.text: bonus depreciation's back. You know, you can you can take all that year one if you want
quote.speaker: Tyler

lessons.lesson: Ask for reviews when customers are getting something free.
